party_source: AEC SenateFirstPrefsByStateByVoteTypeDownload (the party name printed on the ballot); 'Independent' and blank are null.
instruction_source: AEC, 'How to make your vote count' (sample Senate ballot paper), https://www.aec.gov.au/Voting/How_to_vote/files/how-to-make-your-vote-count.pdf, read 2026-10-20.
election: Australian Senate 2019, Australian Capital Territory (above-the-line ballots only, as group rankings)
candidates: D: FRASER ANNING'S CONSERVATIVE NATIONAL PARTY
instruction: Above the line: By numbering at least 6 of these boxes in the order of your choice (with number 1 as your first choice).
notes: Above-the-line ballots only. Each 'candidate' is a party or group box above the line, so a ranking lists boxes, not people. Not a full count of the election. AEC formal preferences file aec-senate-formalpreferences-24310-ACT.zip: 270,231 formal ballot papers, 60,027 below the line and 210,204 above the line. Cleanup follows the Commonwealth Electoral Act 1918 (see data/ausenate/README.md): a below-the-line vote numbering at least 1 to 6 is used as marked, up to the first missing or repeated number; otherwise the above-the-line marks are used the same way. blank_ballots holds all 6,420 informal ballots from the AEC (not only blank ones). Official winners in order of election, from SenateSenatorsElectedDownload. The Senate count uses the weighted inclusive Gregory method with bulk exclusions.
